titre: Rules are no longer enough: the agent needs taste, docs and limits
essentiel: The design system gives the agent its rules, references give it taste: Eno launches marked.dev, a design-reference MCP, and reports 80% fewer back-and-forths.
Making a design system "AI-ready" mostly means finally writing the documentation we already owed humans, as Figma's recommendations show.
On the product side, the question is no longer how powerful the agent is but how autonomous: when it acts, when it asks, when it stops.

syntheses.titre: The design system sets the rules, references bring the taste
syntheses.texte: Maxime Podgorski (Eno) sums up a recurring idea: the design system frames the agent, but references give it taste. AJ sees the same on the code side, where agents recycle the same buttons and gradients until they are plugged into component registries. Shikha Lakhani shows that large teams (Reddit, Stripe, Adobe) build their own prototyping tools for one main reason: so the output finally looks like their brand.

Jessica Trocmé reviews Figma's recommendations for its agent (consistent names, auto layout, descriptions, an examples page) and notes this is what we already owed developers. Loïc Bertetto goes further: his instructions live in written processes that Claude rereads on its own, and laying a design system's foundations drops from a week to a few hours. Both stress the same limit: these processes do not decide for the designer.

syntheses.titre: Design the agent's autonomy, not its power
syntheses.texte: Syed Zubair Ahmed describes an agent interface as a 7-layer control system, from intent to error recovery. Arun Chandra suggests three simple rules: answer on its own, make low-risk changes within set limits, ask for approval before any high-impact decision, with traceable and reversible actions. Jon Barrett reminds us that this control also runs through words, down to the human approval prompt.

syntheses.titre: Design MCPs still hit practical limits
syntheses.texte: Guillaume O. tried to draw screens with Claude Code through Figma's MCP: quotas ran out fast, then Penpot was too slow on a large file, before he found a lighter tool. Meanwhile, the ways to plug agents into components and references keep multiplying (MCP, shadcn CLI, skills). Tooling moves fast, but cost and responsiveness remain deciding factors.

posts.idee: The design system gives the rules, references give the taste. After a year of design executed by agents, Eno turns its internal engine into a tool: marked.dev, an MCP that connects design references to Claude, Codex, Cursor or Figma.

Works with Claude, Codex, Cursor, Figma

References from UI to component animation

posts.role: Senior Product Designer, UX/UI and Figma mentor
posts.idee: AI doesn't invent a new requirement. It exposes the documentation we kept postponing: Figma's recommendations for a design system its AI can read are the ones we already owed humans.
concret: Consistent layer and component names: the AI reads names
Auto layout to express structure and responsive behavior
Reusable components instead of copied screens
Descriptions on components, styles and variables
An "Examples" page in the published library
Example: a button background using a color named "text"
posts.commentaires: Few comments; open question: "everything is documented" or "it's all in my head".

posts.role: Freelance Senior UI/UX Designer, B2B SaaS
posts.idee: I stopped re-explaining my job to AI. His instructions live in written processes (skills) that Claude rereads on its own, with a trigger, the info to request, the steps and the moment it hands back control.
concret: Each process: a description deciding when it activates, info to ask for, steps, references
The design system process rejects wireframes and redirects to UX exploration
Foundations and token naming: from a week to a few hours
Processes stop as soon as a visual or client decision is needed
posts.commentaires: Posted an hour ago, few reactions at reading time.

posts.idee: An agent interface is not a chat screen. It's a 7-layer control system: intent, context, planning, actions, human control, outcomes, transparency and recovery.
concret: Example: planning an offsite for 12 people
Show execution steps before acting
Show completed tasks rather than chat history
Explain blockers and offer alternatives

posts.role: Product Leader, platforms and AI systems
posts.idee: Don't aim for maximum autonomy, aim for appropriate autonomy. Building an agent that acts is an engineering feat; building one that knows when to act, ask or stop is a product feat.
concret: Three rules: answer alone, low-risk changes within set limits, human approval for high-impact decisions
Every action traceable and reversible
Example: a support agent changing an address, issuing a refund or cancelling an order

posts.role: Author of the shikha lakhani newsletter
posts.idee: Build or buy your AI prototyping tool? Reddit, Stripe, Adobe and Miro built their own for one main reason: generic tools don't look like their brand.
concret: Reddit Proto: an MCP maps product components to production code
Prototypes on real data, internal sharing without leak risk
Review markups become targeted edits
Four gaps in standalone tools (v0, Lovable): brand, real data, sharing, code reuse

posts.idee: Coding agents keep recycling the same patterns. To escape generic buttons and gradients, plug them into component libraries and registries they can search, read and install.
concret: 7 resources: Rare UI, Cult UI, 21st.dev, Magic UI, Aceternity UI, NS-UI, React Bits
Three ways to connect: MCP, shadcn CLI, dedicated skills
React Bits Pro: registry, install skill and MCP support

posts.idee: Figma's MCP quotas run out fast once an agent chains actions. To draw screens with Claude Code, this developer moved from Figma to Penpot, then to FigCraft, lighter on a large file.
concret: Figma MCP: call quotas reached quickly, even on a paid plan
Penpot: full MCP but slow rendering on dozens of light and dark screens
FigCraft: lighter rendering engine, MCP server
Work already done in Penpot still has to be migrated

posts.idee: Controlling an agent also runs through words. The article follows a checkout, from the vague "Invalid input" error to an agent's human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval prompt.
concret: One clearer sentence fixes a card number in seconds
UX writing for AI and Claude Design
From error messages to style guides
